name: Ahaz
overview: Ahaz was a male descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, identified specifically as the son of Micah according to 1 Chronicles 8:35. There are no additional notes provided about his life or character in this profile. His lineage places him within the historical context of Israel's tribal divisions.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahaz means 'he has grasped' and is a proper name mentioned in 1 Chronicles 8:35. This name is not indicated as being given by God, but it reflects a personal designation within the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Ahaz was the son of Micah (1 Chronicles 8:35) and the father of Jehoaddah (1 Chronicles 8:36). These explicit family connections situate him within a generational line in the tribe of Benjamin.
scriptureSignificance: Ahaz is notable in the biblical narrative as an example of spiritual failure and misplaced trust. Though descended from a godly heritage, he turned away from God, engaging in idolatry and other sinful practices. His reliance on foreign powers rather than God brought negative consequences for his people, illustrating the dangers of forsaking divine guidance.
